First, we substitute $u={x}^{3}+2.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u={x}^{2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to -\infty $ when $x\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={x}^{3}+2$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $-3$ | $-\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-25$ | $-\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{-3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{({x}^{3}+2)}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-25}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{({x}^{3}+2)}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-25}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u. \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-25}{u}^{-2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-{u}^{-1}]}_{a}^{-25} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{u}]}_{a}^{-25} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-25)}-\frac{1}{a}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(-\frac{1}{25}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{75}.\end{aligned}
$$
